{{nihongo|'''Sugata Shrine'''|菅田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Sugata Shrine''' (すがたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Hachijō-chō, {{ill|Yamatokōriyama|Q118213|qid=Q118213}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}.

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of {{ill|Soejimo district|Q11560415|qid=Q11560415}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1273537/1/44 |title=Engishiki |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. It is regarded nationwide as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} (principal shrine) of the god of {{ill|Metalsmith|Q838566|qid=Q838566}}.

In ancient times, the shrine was located about 300 meters south of its present site, and it is said to have been transferred to its current location around the 3rd year of {{ill|Daiei (era)|fa|دایئی (دوره)|fr|Ère Daiei|ia|Daiei (era)|ja|大永|ko|다이에이 (연호)|no|Daiei (japansk æra)|ru|Тайэй|simple|Daiei (era)|sr|Даиеи (ера)|sv|Daiei (japansk era)|tr|Daiei (dönem)|zh|大永|qid=Q1193564}} (1523)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://jun-yu-roku.com/yamato-heguri-hachijo-sugata/ |title=Sugata Shrine |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>.

=== History ===
Long ago, a beautiful goddess appeared from “Sugata Pond” in Nikaidō, {{ill|Tenri, Nara|Q502196|qid=Q502196}}. She rested for a while in Kagurada in Hachijō-chō, Yamatokōriyama City, and then went westward and took up residence there. Overnight, the place became a dense pine grove, and people began to call the area “Ichiya-matsu” (One-Night Pine). Thus, the present Sugata Shrine—also known as “Ichiya-matsu Tenjin” or “Hachijō Tenjin Shrine”—came to be enshrined there<ref>From the shrine notice board</ref>. The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji Jinja Shiryō}} records: “The Saho River flows to the west, overlooking the banks of Sugata Pond. In the *Horigawa Hyakushu*<ref group="note">A poetry anthology from the late Heian period, likely compiled around the 2nd year of Chōji (1105).</ref>, it is written: ‘The lotus leaves on Sugata Pond, where the maiden dwells, bloom with a gentle heart.’ From this one may know that it was a place of scenic beauty.”

=== Overview ===
The enshrined deity is Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto. There is also a theory that the deity is {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|Q10016750|qid=Q10016750}}, an ancestor of Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto and regarded as a god of blacksmithing<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/815494/1/11 |title=Shingi Shiryō |access-date=2024-4-24}}</ref>. However, the {{ill|jinjameisaichou|Q11590704|qid=Q11590704}} of {{ill|Heguri district|Q11483501|qid=Q11483501}} (Hachijō Village in the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}} was under the jurisdiction of Heguri District and {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|Q971003|qid=Q971003}}, and was incorporated into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōriyama Town}} in 1953) records Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto as the enshrined deity<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://meta01.library.pref.nara.jp/opac/repository/repo/69/ |title=Heguri District Shrine Registry |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>. Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto is the ancestor of the Sugata clan, and the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}} states: “The Sugata no Obito are descendants of {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|Q10016750|qid=Q10016750|lt=Ame-no-Kushi-mahito-tsu-no-Mikoto}}.”

Before the early modern period, the shrine was also called Hachijō Tenjin Shrine or Ichiya-matsu Tenjin, and it enshrined {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}. A legend tells of a miracle in which a pine tree grew overnight, and part of the bark of the Ichiya Pine is {{ill|Votive offering|Q2601788|qid=Q2601788}} in the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yamatotk.web.fc2.com/kouriyama/sugata.htm |title=Sugata Shrine |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>. A stone lantern from the 5th year of {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} (1619) bears the inscription “Ichiya-matsu Kinrin-gū,” suggesting the existence of a {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} called Ichiya-matsu Kinrin-ji. Its location is estimated to have been west of Kasuga Shrine in Nikaidō Kita-Sugata-chō, {{ill|Tenri, Nara|Q502196|qid=Q502196}}<ref group="note">Originally, “it was probably dedicated to Ame-no-Kushi-hitotsu-no-Mikoto” (from *Tenri City History*).</ref><ref name=":01">Tenri City History, Volume 1</ref>.

The {{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}} is built in the {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} style, with a {{ill|Heiden (Shinto)|Q3076699|qid=Q3076699}} installed between it and the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}. In front of the main hall stands a stone lantern inscribed “Before the Deity of Tenmangū,” indicating that the shrine was associated with {{ill|Tenjin faith|Q66890725|qid=Q66890725}}.

It is also thought to form a pair with {{ill|Sugatahime Shrine|Q134893097|qid=Q134893097}}, another Shikinaisha of Soekami District located in Tsutsui-chō, Yamatokōriyama City (enshrining Sugata-hime-no-Mikoto and Ame-no-Kushi-mahito-tsu-no-Mikoto, two deities<ref>According to *Tokusen Shinmeichō* and the National Diet Library Search “Research on Shikinaisha, Vol. 2.”</ref>)<ref group="note">However, the Soekami District Shrine Registry lists only one deity: Izunome-no-Kami.</ref>.

=== Annual festival ===
It was formerly held on October 28, but is now held on October 15.

It is jointly celebrated by Minami-Sugata, Kita-Sugata, Hachijō, Chōan-ji, Miyadō, Nukatabe, Nishimura, and other areas. During the {{ill|procession|Q11561919|qid=Q11561919}} of the hosting household, it is customary for the Sugata clan of Minami-Sugata to proceed first<ref name=":01" />.
